title: Bugonia
synopsis: Two cousins have abducted a pharmaceutical CEO they're convinced is an alien queen. You're the CEO. You have until the lunar eclipse to convince them otherwise — or convince yourself they're right.

nodes.text: You wake duct-taped to a chair in a basement that smells like old paint. Two men sit across from you on lawn chairs. The older one, Teddy, is calm. The younger one, Don, is sweating.

choices.text: Stay silent until they speak
choices.consequence: Read the room.

choices.text: Ask why you are here
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Direct—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Teddy reads, off a printout, the case against you. Your company's drugs have killed thousands. He has paperwork. He has names. He has, he says, photographic evidence that you are 'not from here.'

choices.text: Engage with the drug accusation only
choices.consequence: Find common ground.

choices.text: Engage with the alien accusation seriously
choices.consequence: Meet them where they are.

nodes.text: Don looks at you the way a child looks at a TV he doesn't quite understand. He says, 'I told him you didn't really look like a queen.' Teddy ignores him.

choices.text: Talk to Don as the weaker link
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Tactical.

choices.text: Refuse to triangulate; speak to both
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Strategic—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Teddy explains: there is a lunar eclipse in 36 hours, and he believes the eclipse will 'reveal' your true form. If it does, they will kill you. If it doesn't, they will release you.

choices.text: Negotiate for safer terms
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Bargain.

choices.text: Accept the deadline and use it
choices.consequence: Use the clock.

nodes.text: You learn, in fragments, that Teddy's mother died in a clinical trial sponsored by your company. The trial was, on paper, ethical. The reality is, you suspect, more complicated.

choices.text: Tell him you'll look into the trial personally
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Tell him you'll look into the trial personally” back. Sincerity shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Tell him you're sorry
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Tell him you're sorry” back. Empathy first shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Don, against Teddy's orders, gives you a phone to call your assistant. You have ninety seconds. You realize that 'call for rescue' and 'call to apologize to your team' are, oddly, the same call.

choices.text: Call to apologize and resign
choices.consequence: Use the moment.

choices.text: Send a coded message for rescue
choices.consequence: Use the moment differently.

nodes.text: Teddy has written a manifesto. He reads it to you over many hours. It is, in places, terrifyingly accurate about your industry. It is, in places, deeply unwell about extraterrestrials. You realize that both can be true at once.

choices.text: Critique the manifesto sincerely
choices.consequence: “Critique the manifesto sincerely” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honest reader.

choices.text: Praise the parts that are right
choices.consequence: You commit to “Praise the parts that are right.” The story records the instinct as “Coalition” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Don, who has been silent for hours, finally says, 'I just want my brother to be okay.' You realize Teddy is his brother, that the manifesto is a survival mechanism, and that everything they have done is, in its terrible way, love.

choices.text: Try to give Teddy a kinder story
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Care.

choices.text: Try to get Don to make the call himself
choices.consequence: Use the gap.

nodes.text: Your sister, who knows you are missing, manages to text Don a question. He answers without thinking. The question reveals, accidentally, exactly where you are. You realize Don has, accidentally, saved you.

choices.text: Use the information to plan an escape
choices.consequence: You commit to “Use the information to plan an escape.” The story records the instinct as “Logical” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Use the information to negotiate, not escape
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Patient.

nodes.text: You spend the next twelve hours in the basement having the most honest conversation of your professional life — about drug trials, about pricing, about the small terrible decisions that compound into bodies. You realize, in passing, that you might be a worse person than you'd believed.

choices.text: Confess to Teddy fully
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Confess to Teddy fully” back. Truth shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Confess only the parts you can change
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Pragmatic truth.

nodes.text: Your sister has, with help, called the FBI. They are, you understand from a small radio Don turns on by accident, in a perimeter outside. The eclipse is in nine hours.

choices.text: Encourage Teddy to surrender
choices.consequence: Help him save himself.

choices.text: Stay calm; wait for them
choices.consequence: “Stay calm; wait for them” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Patience.

nodes.text: The moon's shadow crosses the sun. Teddy stares at you with an intensity you have never had pointed at you. You do not, of course, transform. He blinks. The deadline passes.

choices.text: Stay calm and offer him a way out
choices.consequence: “Stay calm and offer him a way out” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: De-escalate.

choices.text: Beg him to release you now, before the FBI escalates
choices.consequence: You commit to “Beg him to release you now, before the FBI escalates.” The story records the instinct as “Urgent” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Don, off-camera, walks upstairs and opens the front door of the cabin. The FBI agent at the door has been speaking gently for hours. Don sits on the porch with his hands up and tells them, plainly, the layout of the basement.

choices.text: Use the moment to convince Teddy
choices.consequence: Window of mercy.

choices.text: Stay still until the agents arrive
choices.consequence: Don't break it.

nodes.text: Teddy and Don are arrested. The case becomes, briefly, national. You testify. You also, the same year, voluntarily resign from your company and spend three years working with regulators on patient-trial reforms.

choices.text: Visit Teddy in prison
choices.consequence: Bear the weight.

choices.text: Send Teddy books, not visits
choices.consequence: Care at distance.

nodes.text: Two months later you write a resignation letter that is also a kind of confession. You leave a foundation behind. You leave the equity behind. You realize, looking at the empty drawer, that the basement clarified something the office never could.

choices.text: Start a new company aimed at patient safety
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Start a new company aimed at patient safety” back. Action shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Take a year off entirely
choices.consequence: You commit to “Take a year off entirely.” The story records the instinct as “Recover” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You visit Teddy in prison. He is, by then, on medication that takes the edges off. He does not, at first, want to see you. The third visit he says, 'I still think you're wrong about most things.' You laugh. He almost does too.

choices.text: Stay involved in his case for parole
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Long—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Visit but not advocate
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Limited.

nodes.text: The foundation you set up funds independent trial monitors. It is, by every measurement, more effective than your company ever was. You realize, late, that maybe you should have been doing this all along. You also realize there is no point in regretting it instead of doing it.

choices.text: Lead the foundation
choices.consequence: You commit to “Lead the foundation.” The story records the instinct as “Continue” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Hire someone better suited and step back
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Cede.

nodes.text: Don is in a halfway house, working at a grocery store, mostly steady. You visit. He thanks you for not pressing charges on him personally. You realize repair is, partly, the work of small visits.

choices.text: Visit Don monthly
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Steady.

choices.text: Visit when he asks
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Visit when he asks” back. Reactive shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: An industry conference asks you to keynote. You almost decline. You decide, instead, to tell the basement story plainly. The room is, for a long moment, silent. The reform you push from that stage, for once, lands.

choices.text: Use the platform yearly
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Voice—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Use it once and step back
choices.consequence: You commit to “Use it once and step back.” The story records the instinct as “One arrow” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: On the night the eclipse would have happened, you sit outside and watch the sky. Teddy is not, in fact, watching it from his cell. He is asleep. You realize the curse, the basement, the manifesto, were always a metaphor he believed because nothing else explained his grief. You decide what to do next.

choices.text: Keep repairing
choices.consequence: You commit to “Keep repairing.” The story records the instinct as “Active repair” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Keep distance
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Keep distance” back. Mature distance shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You spend the rest of your career trying to repair what your earlier career did. The math doesn't quite balance. You decide it's enough that you're trying. The basement, when you remember it, is not a nightmare — it's the moment your life turned the right way around.

You stop being a public figure. The foundation does well. Teddy gets parole. He never quite forgives you. You never quite forgive yourself either. You both live anyway. It is, you decide, the honest kind of recovery.
